newsitem.title: USA: Sugar an issue in US-Mexico ag trade - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Sugar an issue in US-Mexico ag trade - Glickman.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman described a "positive" and "upbeat" state of U.S.-Mexico agricultural trade Thursday but said sugar was a problem area.

Glickman spent more than two hours in briefing farm-state lawmakers on last week's binational meeting. A handful of agreements were announced during the consultation involving broader trade in pork, wheat and citrus.
"Sugar is a problem area," Glickman told reporters aferward, that was raised by Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo in high-level discussions.
Under the North American Free Trade Agreement, Mexico is limited at present to shipping 25,000 tonnes of sugar to U.S. buyers annually.
"They would like to see it increased," Glickman said. "They would like to see us revisit this issue."
The U.S. trade representative has jurisdiction over the issue "but we talked about it as well," Glickman said.

Glickman said at the briefing he "talked about the positive nature of U.S. agricultural trade with Mexico, about $5.5 billion worth of exports into Mexico, which is a substantial increase over previous years, a record level... "
House Agriculture Committee chairman Bob Smith, Oregon Republican, said there were still some "irritants" but U.S.-Mexico trade "is really going very well."
"In the long run, it is still a very valuable market for us," Smith said.
At the binational meeting, agreements were announced allowing pork from Sonora and wheat from the Mexicali valley into the United States and citrus from Florida and Arizona into Mexico.
Texan Charles Stenholm, Democratic leader on the committee, said Glickman's briefing was "upbeat" and optimistic.
